title: Singing and dancing in a children's movie prologue at age nine
summary: Herman says his father steered him toward theatre; he did his first tour at nine singing and dancing in a kid unit doing a prologue to the film School Days, and used the money to buy a saxophone.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well, I'd like to talk to you about your early dates first, so we can do this on a somewhat chronological, developmental order for the archives of the Smithsonian Institute.
Could you discuss how you got started, how did it really begin for you? That is, your motivations and early training?

Well, it's very difficult, really, because I've lived a long time, I can't remember the earliest things, but I still recollect the fact that my father and mother were very interested in my having some sort of musical career, preferably in the theatre.

And with this in mind, my father, who I guess was a frustrated singer, to some degree, decided I would be the completion of his ambitions. And so he taught me to sing and later I studied a little bit of dancing. But his whole intent was to make me a performer of one kind of another, and I guess he must have been able to do that, because I did my first tour when I was nine years old. And with some of the money I earned from that tour, which was a summertime tour, I was able to buy a saxophone and then later, a clarinet.
What were you doing on that tour?
And it was a kid unit.

Yeah, a unit of young children. And we were doing a prologue to a movie. And the movie was a Booth Tarkington story, called "School Days," which -- I guess he had made his reputation with "Penrod" and "Penrod and Simon" and those things for a movie for a child. A young man starred in the silent motion pictures by the name of Wesley Barry. [Berry]
And actually, what I was supposedly doing was playing the part of -- in the prologue, of Wesley Barry. And -- who was a frecklefaced kid, and I don't know where these thoughts came from --
-- that I had to sing and dance, along with other kids.
